items.question: Co to jest ETR?
items.text: ETR to szacowany czas przywrócenia zasilania, czyli informacja, kiedy klienci znów mają mieć prąd. Na platformie nie znalazłem jednak jednej, ogólnej definicji tego skrótu w danych o ekipach, awariach i czasach przywracania, więc nie będę zgadywać więcej. Najbliższe są dwa pojęcia: „Global ETR” to moment, gdy prąd wraca u 90% klientów z czasu szczytu awarii (publikacja wymaga podpisu Dowodzenia i Operacji), a „ETR by area” to oszacowanie dla obszaru każdej bazy ekip. Przycisk poniżej otwiera stronę After-action, a zakładka „ETR accuracy” pokazuje, jak bardzo każdy ETR odbiegał od tego, co się stało. Rzeczywisty przebieg jest symulowany, więc to praktyka, a nie dowód z terenu.

items.question: What is a boil-water notice?
items.text:
The documents give no formal definition of a boil-water notice; WQC 07.120 only points to the South Carolina regulation for the definition [1]. In practice, it is a public notice telling customers in an area to boil water used for drinking and cooking [2]. The Water Compliance Officer decides on it with the Water Incident Lead [3]. In Georgia the equivalent is a boil water advisory under WQC 07.114.

Sources:
[1] WQC 07.120 Rev C, 1.0 PURPOSE; 2.0 SCOPE; 3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES; 7.0 RECORDS; 8.0 REFERENCES; ATTACHMENT A NOTICE WORDING (SOUTH CAROLINA), pp. 1-4: "SC R.61-58 (definition 15); SC R.61-58.7.E(7) WDS 03.105; WDS 03.420; WQC 07.114; WQC 07.130; PCN 02.032; F-WQC-031"
[2] WQC 07.120 Rev C, Control box; 7.0 RECORDS; 8.0 REFERENCES; ATTACHMENT A NOTICE WORDING (SOUTH CAROLINA), pp. 1-4: "Due to [cause], customers of SGW in the following area should boil water used for drinking and cooking: [streets and zone]."
[3] WQC 07.120 Rev C, 1.0 PURPOSE; 2.0 SCOPE; 3.0 RESPONSIBILITIES; 7.0 RECORDS; 8.0 REFERENCES; ATTACHMENT A NOTICE WORDING (SOUTH CAROLINA), pp. 1-4: "Water Compliance Officer: decides on the BWN with the Water Incident Lead. Notifies SCDES. Requests release of the notice."

answer.text:
The documents give no formal definition of a boil-water notice; WQC 07.120 only points to the South Carolina regulation for the definition [1]. In practice, it is a public notice telling customers in an area to boil water used for drinking and cooking [2]. The Water Compliance Officer decides on it with the Water Incident Lead [3]. In Georgia the equivalent is a boil water advisory under WQC 07.114.

Sources:

[2] WQC 07.120 Rev C, Control box; 7.0 RECORDS; 8.0 REFERENCES; ATTACHMENT A NOTICE WORDING (SOUTH CAROLINA), pp. 1-4: "Due to [cause], customers of SGW in the following area should boil water used for drinking and cooking: [streets and zone]."
